title: Analytics event taxonomy
description: Shape of schemas/analytics-taxonomy.json — the single list of product events the landing page (Plausible) and the console/API (PostHog EU) are allowed to emit. Two repositories code against it (ADR-006), so the names, the property spellings and the owning issue live in one machine-readable file rather than in two markdown tables that drift.

$schema.description: Relative pointer to this file, so an editor validates the taxonomy as it is typed.

sharedProperties.description: Properties that mean the same thing on more than one event. An event references them by name in `uses`; it may not redefine one.

eventName.description: snake_case, verb-last (`cta_click`, not `click_cta`), so related events sort together.

type.description: Scalars only. A nested object is a property nobody can build a breakdown on, and it is how free text gets in by accident.

required.description: false means the emitter omits it rather than sending null — an absent property and an empty one are different rows in a breakdown.

enum.description: Closed value set. Prefer it: an unbounded string property is a breakdown with one row per visitor.

example.description: A real value, so the readable table shows one. For a closed set it must be a member of `enum`; the taxonomy test checks that.

surface.description: Which of the three surfaces owns the emission. Exactly one — an event emitted from two places is two events.

transport.description: browser = the surface's own script calls the tool directly (landing/Plausible only). server = router-api calls the tool with posthog-node. first-party-ingest = the browser posts it to router-api, which forwards it (ADR-006 §3: the console makes no third-party requests).

owner.description: The issue that implements the emission.

when.description: The exact moment it fires, precise enough that two implementers cannot disagree about whether it fired.

allOf.$comment: Plausible has no server-side event API in our plan, and the console emits nothing to a third party directly.
Nothing router-api computes needs to be reported by a browser.
ADR-006 §3: the console never talks to a third party; its two browser events go through router-api.
